Large language model (LLM)-powered agents can be ac-
curateon averageyet unreliable in production, a discrep-
ancy that has been observed but remains largely unaddressed.
When given thesametask five times, a ReAct agent on the
AppWorld benchmark using GPT-4.1 succeeds in all five runs
only 53% of the time, even though its per-run pass rate aver-
ages 77%. We call this 24-point shortfall theconsistency gap,
and we argue that addressing it is a precondition for trustwor-
thy AI agent deployment. We present a self-evolving agent
framework that reduces this gap by identifying unstable, low-
consistency steps in agent trajectories and converting them
into episodic memory the agent can draw on in future runs.
At its core is aConsistency Analyzerthat pinpoints where
and why a trajectory is likely to flip across executions, and
aGuideline Generatorthat converts the diagnosis into tar-

Contributions.(1) A formalization and empirical charac-
terization of the consistency gap (Section 2). (2) A black-box
Consistency Analyzer (Section 3.1) that estimates step- and
trajectory-level consistency from response variability via
configurable resampling; aggregate trajectory consistency
also correlates with trajectory pass/fail (AUROC0.69), let-
ting it support the generator's own judgment of trajec-
tory outcome where no ground-truth rating is available.
(3) Consistency-targeted guideline generation (Section 3.2)
driven by step-level inconsistency. (4) Empirical results
(Section 4) on AppWorld with ReAct/GPT-4.1 and GPT-
OSS-120B showing+16pp Passˆ5 same-task and+13pp
similar-task generalization

evidence.excerpt:
Self-consistency, inference scaling, and uncertainty
quantification.Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) sam-
ples multiple chains of thought and selects the majority an-
swer; inference-scaling work (Snell et al. 2024) and reason-
ing models such as OpenAI's o1 family generalize the same
intuition, and agent variants use tests or an LLM judge to
select among rolled-out solutions. We differ on two axes:
resampling happensofflinerather than at runtime, and the
objective is consistency, not accuracy - variability is a di-
agnostic signal for where the prompt should be hardened,
not a voting mechanism. Predictive entropy (Malinin and
Gales 2021) overstates uncertainty when responses vary in
wording but agree in meaning, since it measures spread
over surface forms rather than over meaning; semantic en-
tropy (Kuhn, Gal, and Farquhar 2023; Farquhar et al. 2024)
addresses this via clustering; 
[… separate evidence block …]
MemP (Fang et al. 2025), ReasoningBank (Ouyang
et al. 2025), ACE (Zhang et al. 2025a), and Memento (Zhou
et al. 2025) extract reusable workflows from traces, though
naive accumulation can propagate errors (Xiong et al. 2025).
We build on Fang et al. (2026), adding a consistency-
targeted extraction signal atop its storage and retrieval ma-
chinery.
Reliability, reproducibility, and observability.App-
World (Trivedi et al. 2024) is one of several benchmarks
reporting multi-run statistics, and Ye et al. (Ye et al. 2026)
show that such run-to-run variance is itself an underspecified
property of self-improving, memory-based agents, sensitive
to task order and evaluation protocol; our guideline-injection
loop targets exactly this source of fragility. Our Passˆk vs.
Mean@kformulation generalizes pass@kfrom code gen-
eration (Chen et al. 2021) to per-difficulty granularity, and
lands within

Limitations.Our Passˆ5 comparisons assume compa-
rable platform-side non-determinism between baseline and
guideline-injected runs, which we cannot directly measure
or control. We do not claim the framework eliminates in-
consistency (a substantial gap remains, especially on Hard
tasks) or that the analyzer is a verifier: it scoresstability, not
correctness, and a confidently-wrong decision looks consis-
tent to it. Our default resampling budget (N= 30per infer-
ence step) multiplies token cost roughly30×per trajectory;
reducing this cost without degrading guideline quality, e.g.,
via adaptive resampling that concentrates samples on candi-
date flat steps, is an important direction for future work.
evidence.explanation: The limitations section explicitly states these constraints, demonstrating awareness of the framework's boundaries and the conditions under which the results hold. This is a substantive limitation discussion rather than a generic disclaimer.
evidence.paraphrase: The paper acknowledges limitations including the assumption of comparable platform-side non-determinism, the analyzer's inability to detect confidently-wrong decisions, and the 30x token cost of resampling.

support_verification.explanation_reason: The cited appendix text states the tables report the complete per-difficulty breakdown underlying the aggregate numbers discussed in Section 4, and the tables provide the per-difficulty values needed to verify reported improvements.
support_verification.reason: The appendix text explicitly states Tables 1 and 2 report the complete per-difficulty breakdown for baseline, same-task, and similar-task guidelines, and the tables include Pass^5, Mean@5, and Consistency values for both GPT-4.1 and GPT-OSS-120B.

positive_signals: The paper formalizes the consistency gap as the difference between Mean@k and Pass^k, and presents a self-evolving agent framework with a Consistency Analyzer and Guideline Generator to reduce this gap.
The consistency gap is empirically characterized on AppWorld with ReAct/GPT-4.1 and GPT-OSS-120B, showing a 24.4pp gap for GPT-4.1 and 23.8pp for GPT-OSS-120B.

The paper positions its work relative to self-consistency, agentic memory, and reliability literature, distinguishing its offline resampling and consistency-targeted guideline generation from prior approaches.

The paper acknowledges limitations including the assumption of comparable platform-side non-determinism, the analyzer's inability to detect confidently-wrong decisions, and the 30x token cost of resampling.
The paper provides full per-difficulty results in Appendix B tables, including baseline, same-task, and similar-task Pass^5, Mean@5, and Consistency values for both models.
